chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Rabi', from Fuzayl, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Be with the wet-nurses who have clear milk, for the milk transmits [kinship].

key_terms.الْوُضَّاءِ: Plural of wadāʾ, meaning clear, pure, or unadulterated; referring to the quality of the milk.
key_terms.يُعْدِي: Transmits or conveys; here referring to the transmission of foster kinship (radāʿ) status.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of choosing a wet-nurse with 'clear milk' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of the legal principle that 'milk transmits' (al-laban yaʿdi), establishing that a wet-nurse's physical and spiritual purity influences the foster child's lineage and marital eligibility. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the importance of selecting a wet-nurse not just for nourishment but to ensure the validity of nasab (lineage) and to avoid unintended mahram relationships that would prohibit marriage. The reference to 'clear milk' (al-wudāʾ) reflects the scholarly emphasis on the quality and purity of the nurse as a factor in the sanctity of the foster bond.
